title: Convert incident runbook actions into degradation tolerance and rollback acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Translate concrete actions from the KV-cache hot-region postmortem into PRD-level requirements: explicit degradation windows, deterministic rollback acceptance tests, canary gating, and operator runbook verification criteria. Background: The Feb outage revealed gaps where engineering runbook steps did not map to product acceptance criteria. This ticket scopes a PRD update to ensure future rollouts and runtime changes carry testable, observable safety contracts. Goals: 1) Surface specific runbook actions as immutable acceptance gates in PRDs; 2) Define measurable degradation tolerances (latency percentiles, error budgets, throughput floors) and corresponding rollback triggers; 3) Add synthetic and canary checks that validate rollback/fallback paths; 4) Ensure runbook verifications are included in release acceptance and automated test suites. Out of scope: changes to the serving runtime implementation (those will be separate ENG tickets), commercial SLA changes, and dedicated capacity pricing implications.
acceptance_criteria: PRD updated with a new 'Operational Safety Contracts' section mapping at least 6 postmortem runbook actions to product-level requirements
Each mapped requirement has: a) measurable SLI/SLO (units and thresholds), b) explicit rollback gate, and c) test coverage (manual or automated)
Define three degradation profiles (partial KV cache regen, cross-region latency spike, sustained kernel slowdown) with concrete thresholds and mitigation sequences
Add two canary checks in the release checklist: synthetic end-to-end generation at 95th percentile latency and KV-cache warmup verification; both must pass for canary to promote
Acceptance tests added to the QA suite and smoke run for every runtime release; test failures automatically block release in the release pipeline
All links to runbook playbooks, incident postmortem, and test plans included in PRD; at least one stakeholder sign-off from Eng, SRE, and Security
decisions: Use 'degradation profile' terminology in the PRD to avoid conflating with SLAs
Adopt three-tier rollback gates (Immediate Abort, Canary Pause, Gradual Rollback) mapped to severity levels in the runbook
Require an automated synthetic check for KV cache correctness to be part of the canary stage before traffic shift
Include explicit operator verification steps in PRD (who to contact, required dashboards, and playbook link) rather than generic 'notify SRE' language
tradeoffs: Stricter release gates increase release friction and time-to-production for minor runtime improvements
Automating all runbook checks requires additional engineering effort up front but reduces on-call load and incident blast radius long-term
Defining hard thresholds may cause false positives during atypical traffic patterns; mitigation is to couple thresholds with trend-based heuristics and require two independent signals before rollback
